hero.title: RAG systems: AI that answers from your company's documents
hero.subtitle: A RAG system is an AI that, before answering, searches your company's documents —manuals, contracts, policies— and replies with what it found, citing the source.
hero.pilotNote: {pilotWeeks}-week pilot with your documents: {pilotPrice}, one-time payment, plus VAT if applicable.

intro.title: What is RAG? An AI knowledge base, in plain words
intro.subtitle: RAG stands for retrieval augmented generation: answers generated from a search across your documents. In practice, it is a chatbot built on your company's documents that does not answer from memory but by looking up your files.

ask.title: Ask the way you would ask a colleague
ask.desc: “How many vacation days do I get?” or “What does the contract with this supplier say about penalties?”. No more digging folder by folder.

search.title: The AI searches your documents, not the internet
search.desc: It only looks at the documents your company chooses to load, so answers follow your policies instead of some random web page.

cite.title: It answers and shows you where it came from
cite.desc: Every answer includes the citation from the document so you can check it. If the information is not in your documents, it tells you.

intro.analogy: Think of it as a new employee who has read every company manual and, every time they answer, shows you the paragraph they took it from.

sectors.title: Use cases by industry
sectors.subtitle: A chatbot built on your company's documents helps wherever people waste time looking for information in manuals, contracts or regulations.

how.title: How retrieval augmented generation (RAG) works
how.subtitle: Four steps between your documents and a cited answer.
how.diagramLabel: Diagram: documents, index, search and cited answer

docs.title: Documents
docs.desc: We extract the text from your PDF, Word, TXT files or web pages and split it into paragraph-based passages. Each passage remembers which document it came from.

index.title: Index
index.desc: Passages are stored in a search index on the server. The AI model is not retrained: your documents live in the index, not inside the model.

search.title: Search
search.desc: For each question, the system retrieves the most relevant passages (the “retrieval”). In the demo, search is keyword-based (BM25): it finds the passages that share words with your question and keeps the top 5.

answer.title: Cited answer
answer.desc: A language model (GPT-4o mini from OpenAI by default) writes the answer from those passages and tags each fact with [1], [2]… so you can open the source.

example.title: Illustrative example
example.question: How far in advance do I need to request vacation?
example.answer: You must request it in writing from your direct manager at least 15 business days in advance [1].
example.sourceQuote: “Vacation must be requested in writing from the direct manager at least 15 business days in advance…”

security.title: Security and privacy of your documents
security.subtitle: This is what the system does today with your documents and your questions.

storage.title: Where your documents are stored
storage.desc: On KopTup's server, hosted on Railway, with a MongoDB database. That is where we extract the text, split it into passages and build the search index; questions and answers are also logged there. These providers, like OpenAI, may process data outside Colombia, mainly in the United States (see the privacy policy).

provider.title: Which AI provider we use
provider.desc: OpenAI, through its API. The default model is GPT-4o mini. The OpenAI access key stays on our server: it never reaches the browser.

sent.title: What is sent to OpenAI
sent.desc: Only what is needed to write each answer: your question, the most relevant passages (not the whole document), the assistant's instructions and the latest messages of the conversation.

training.title: Your documents do not train the AI
training.desc: Under OpenAI's current API policy, data sent through the API is not used to train its models by default. OpenAI may keep it for up to 30 days to detect abuse.

control.title: If you need more control
control.desc: In the Professional plan we build role-based permissions in your project, and Enterprise is deployed on your cloud or your own servers (on-premise), with company sign-in (SSO) and auditing also built in your project. On every plan, each answer is written through OpenAI's API: the question and the relevant passages are sent to OpenAI.

demo.title: In the public demo
demo.desc: In “Try your own document”, the file is processed only in the server's memory (it is not saved to disk or to a database), and the document, its index and the conversation are deleted 1 hour after upload. We only keep your email, with your authorization, and the document's type and length, not its content. Even so, do not upload confidential information.

accuracy.title: How we avoid made-up answers
accuracy.subtitle: An AI that makes up answers is worse than no AI at all. That is why the system follows three rules.

onlyDocs.title: Instructed to answer only from your documents
onlyDocs.desc: The model receives the passages found in your documents and the instruction to rely on them, not on what it “knows” from the internet. That is why every answer comes with its citation: so you can check it.

cites.title: It cites the source
cites.desc: Every answer shows which document and chunk it comes from, so you can check it before using it.

notFound.title: It says “I couldn't find that information”
notFound.desc: When the answer is not in your documents, it says so instead of guessing. Those questions show you which document is missing.

accuracy.measure: And we measure it: the pilot includes an accuracy report with 50 test questions about your own documents.

integrations.title: Integrations: Google Drive, SharePoint, WhatsApp, databases and APIs
integrations.subtitle: In your project we build the connection between the assistant and where your documents already live, and the channels your people already use. Today the demo works with files you upload (PDF, DOCX, TXT) and web pages.

drive.title: Google Drive
drive.desc: A connector built in your project to use Google Drive folders as the assistant's source.

sharepoint.title: SharePoint
sharepoint.desc: A connector built in your project for your company's SharePoint document libraries.

whatsapp.title: WhatsApp
whatsapp.desc: A channel built in your project with the official WhatsApp Business API: your customers or team ask on WhatsApp and get the answer with its source. Meta's messaging fees are billed separately, at cost.

databases.title: Databases
databases.desc: In your project we connect the assistant to your databases so it can also query that information.

apis.title: APIs
apis.desc: In your project we bring the answers to your intranet, CRM or apps through an API.

integrations.note: The number of document origins depends on the plan: one in Essential, up to three in Professional and unlimited in Enterprise. The WhatsApp channel is built in your project from the Professional plan.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about RAG systems

whatIsRag.a: RAG (retrieval augmented generation) is a technique that combines a search engine with a language model: it first finds the chunks of your documents that answer the question, and then the AI writes the answer with that information, citing the source. It works like an AI knowledge base you can ask in natural language.

vsChatgpt.q: How is it different from ChatGPT?
vsChatgpt.a: ChatGPT answers with what it learned during training and does not know your company's internal documents. A RAG system first searches your documents, answers with what it finds there and shows you the source; plus, you decide which documents it uses. To write the answers we use OpenAI models, from the company behind ChatGPT, through its API.

training.q: Are my documents used to train the AI?
training.a: No. We do not train any model with your documents: the system looks them up for each question and only sends OpenAI the question, the relevant chunks and the latest messages of the conversation. Under OpenAI's current API policy, data sent through the API is not used to train its models by default; OpenAI may keep it for up to 30 days to detect abuse, or longer if the law requires it.

notFound.q: What happens if the answer is not in my documents?
notFound.a: The assistant tells you “I couldn't find that information” instead of making up an answer. Those questions help you spot which documents are missing: once you load them, the assistant can answer.

synonyms.a: The demo searches by keywords: if you ask with words that are not in the document (for example, “term” when the contract says “deadline”), it may answer “not found”. In the pilot we measure this with your 50 real questions, written in your team's vocabulary, and the report shows which ones it did not find.

pilotInput.q: What do I need to provide for the pilot?
pilotInput.a: Up to 100 documents from a single origin, 50 real questions from your team with the answer you expect, and someone to review the answers with us. We start with a 30-minute call, and in {pilotWeeks} weeks you get the assistant with your documents and the accuracy report: how many it answered correctly, with which source, and how many it said “not found”.

formats.a: PDF with text, Word (DOCX), TXT and web pages. Depending on the plan, in your project we also build the connection to Google Drive or SharePoint and to databases or APIs. If your PDFs are scans (images without text), we review it with you during the pilot.

whatsapp.a: Yes, from the Professional plan: in your project we build the WhatsApp channel with the official WhatsApp Business API, and the assistant answers there and on your website. The demo on this site works only on the web. Meta's WhatsApp messaging fees are billed separately, at cost.

cost.a: The {pilotWeeks}-week pilot costs {pilotPrice}, one-time (with 19% VAT: {pilotPriceVat}); if you sign up for a plan within the following 30 days, it is fully deducted from the implementation. The Essential plan costs {essentialSetup} for implementation plus {essentialMonthly} per month (first year: {essentialFirstYear}); Professional, {proSetup} for implementation plus {proMonthly} per month (first year: {proFirstYear}); and Enterprise starts at {enterpriseSetup}, with a monthly fee based on the service level we agree on. All prices are plus VAT if applicable; the proposal confirms whether your case carries it.

time.a: The pilot with your documents takes {pilotWeeks} weeks. Implementation takes {essentialWeeks} weeks on the Essential plan, {proWeeks} weeks on Professional and {enterpriseWeeks} weeks on Enterprise.

salud.name: Healthcare
salud.title: AI that answers from your protocols, regulations and payer contracts, citing the source
salud.subtitle: An assistant for clinics, providers and health insurers: your team asks in natural language and gets the answer with the passage from the protocol, regulation or contract it comes from. This is called a RAG system.
salud.cardDesc: Clinical protocols, healthcare regulations and medical claims auditing, with the source cited.

cases.title: Clinical protocols
cases.desc: Care staff look up internal guidelines and protocols in natural language and see the document passage behind each answer.

cases.title: Healthcare regulations
cases.desc: The resolutions, circulars and regulatory manuals you upload, in a single knowledge base, with the regulation and the passage that support each answer.

cases.title: Lookups for medical claims auditing
cases.desc: Your auditors ask the assistant what the contract, fee schedule or denial manual says while reviewing an invoice, and see the cited clause. The assistant answers questions; it does not review invoices on its own.

salud.disclaimer: The AI supports your team with cited information; clinical and audit decisions remain with your professionals.
salud.heroDemo: Try the demo with a sample clinic
salud.demoNote: In the demo, the sample clinic answers questions from patients (tests, appointments and rights) and from the medical claims team (filing and denials) with fictitious documents. To try it with one of your manuals or contracts, use “Try it with your document”, with no patient data.

example.question: What is the internal deadline to answer a denial?
example.answer: Within 10 working days of receiving it [1].
example.sourceQuote: “The medical claims team answers each denial within 10 working days of receiving it…”

data.title: Your data and your patients' data
data.desc: To start, we recommend documents without patient data: protocols, regulations, contracts and fee schedules. If you want to query documents with patient data, we review it with you before the pilot. Documents stay on KopTup's server and, to write each answer, the question and the relevant passages are sent to OpenAI; these providers may process data outside Colombia, mainly in the United States.

notFound.title: If the answer is not in your documents
notFound.desc: The assistant replies “I couldn't find that information in the uploaded documents” instead of guessing. It is instructed not to use outside knowledge, and every answer comes with its citation so your team can check it.

related.title: Need a system that reviews invoices?
related.desc: That is a different product: the Healthcare expert system, which applies audit rules with a sample fee schedule, flags potential denials and uses AI to extract invoice data. It is not the assistant on this page and is quoted separately.
related.ctaRequest: Request access to the expert system demo

legal.name: Legal
legal.title: AI for law firms and legal teams: ask your contracts and get the clause cited
legal.subtitle: Your team asks in natural language about contracts, internal legal opinions, regulations and rulings the firm uploads, and gets the answer with the clause or passage it comes from. This is called a RAG system.
legal.cardDesc: Search contracts with AI, internal legal opinions and regulations, with the clause cited.

cases.title: Contracts
cases.desc: Find what each contract says about terms, penalties, renewals or confidentiality, with the clause cited and without reading it end to end.

cases.title: Internal legal opinions
cases.desc: Reuse the opinions and memos your team has already written: the assistant finds them and shows you the original document.

cases.title: Regulations and case law
cases.desc: The laws, decrees and rulings your team already has and uploads, with the passage that supports each answer. If a ruling isn't uploaded, the assistant won't cite it: it tells you it couldn't find it.

legal.disclaimer: The assistant speeds up the search; legal interpretation stays with your lawyers.
legal.heroDemo: Try the demo with a sample law firm
legal.demoNote: In the demo, the sample law firm has a model agreement and an internal case file manual (fictitious documents). Try the last suggested question: it is not in the documents, and you will see that the assistant does not make up a ruling.

example.question: How long does the confidentiality obligation last?
example.answer: For the term of the agreement and for 3 years after its termination [1].
example.sourceQuote: “This obligation lasts for the term of the agreement and for 3 years after its termination.”

data.title: Confidentiality
data.desc: Your documents are stored on KopTup's server. Only the question and the relevant passages, never the whole document, go to OpenAI, which under its current API policy does not use them for training. These providers may process data outside Colombia, mainly in the United States. If your firm needs a confidentiality agreement, tell us when you request a quote.

notFound.title: What if it cites a ruling that doesn't exist?
notFound.desc: The assistant only works with the documents your firm uploads and is instructed not to use outside knowledge. If a law or ruling isn't uploaded, it replies “I couldn't find that information in the uploaded documents”. Every answer shows the exact passage so you can check it; final review stays with your lawyers.

soporte.name: Support
soporte.title: AI assistant for internal manuals and customer support
soporte.subtitle: Your agents ask about manuals, policies and the knowledge base in natural language, and answer customers with the current policy and its source. This is called a RAG system.
soporte.cardDesc: An AI assistant for internal manuals, policies and your agents' knowledge base.

cases.title: Manuals
cases.desc: Procedures, product manuals and technical guides one question away, with the manual passage that supports each answer.

cases.title: Policies
cases.desc: Warranties, returns, delivery times or commercial terms: your whole team answers with the same current policy, not the version each person remembers.

cases.title: Knowledge base for agents
cases.desc: New agents find answers without interrupting senior ones, and the knowledge base is updated when you add or change documents.

soporte.heroDemo: Try the demo with a sample store
soporte.demoNote: In the demo, the sample store has its returns, shipping and warranty policies (fictitious documents): ask as a customer would, for example about a shipping cost or an exchange.

example.question: How long is the furniture warranty?
example.answer: 12 months against manufacturing defects, counted from delivery [1].
example.sourceQuote: “Furniture has a 12-month warranty against manufacturing defects, counted from delivery.”

data.title: Your data
data.desc: Your manuals and policies are stored on KopTup's server; to write each answer, the question and the relevant passages are sent to OpenAI, which under its current API policy does not use them for training. If you put the chat on your website, anyone who visits it can ask it questions, so use it with documents that can be public.

notFound.title: If the answer is not in your documents
notFound.desc: The assistant replies “I couldn't find that information in the uploaded documents” instead of making up a policy. Those questions show you which document is missing.
